body: J.C. Hart Co. and Chase Development proposed The Elements, a $61 million apartment project on the former Willows Event Center property at 6729 Westfield Blvd., north of Broad Ripple. The Metropolitan Development Commission voted 8-0 on December 20, 2023 to approve a rezoning for 192 apartments and 16 town houses, sending it to the City-County Council for final adoption, the Indianapolis Business Journal reported.

Oxbow Estates Homeowners Association, Spirit Lake Co-owners Association and two individuals with property abutting the site then sued the MDC, the developers and property owner Evergreen LLC in Marion County Superior Court. They argued the commission did not consider a 2003 set of commitments for property around Spirit Lake that limits density to 1.94 units per acre and can be enforced by owners within two properties or 660 feet of the rezoned land. The project covers 21.4 acres counting Spirit Lake, or about 8 acres without it, according to the IBJ. The neighbors said they would accept up to 144 units. J.C. Hart chairman John Hart called the suit "unfortunate" and said the claims were meritless.

The project had already been scaled back once: Hart announced it in late 2021 with 256 apartments and 18 townhouses and withdrew the plan in mid-2022 amid opposition from nearby residents, the IBJ reported. On February 5, 2024, about 20 minutes into the council meeting, the developer and the neighbors reached a deal for 168 apartments with no condos or town houses, fewer ancillary buildings, a two-acre park, and a commitment from Hart not to develop other property it controls around Spirit Lake for at least five years after occupancy begins. The council approved the rezoning 24-0, with one abstention.

The IBJ reported the lawsuit was expected to be dismissed with prejudice the next day; we have not confirmed the dismissal. Hart said in a statement that the company is "grateful that we have been able to work effectively with our neighbors."

timeline.label: J.C. Hart Co. and Chase Development announce the project
The developers withdraw the plan amid neighborhood opposition
The Metropolitan Development Commission approves a 192-apartment, 16-town-house rezoning, 8-0
Neighborhood associations and abutting owners sue in Marion County Superior Court over the 2003 density commitments
Sides reach a deal for 168 apartments; the City-County Council approves it 24-0
